title: Ninety Days
what: A game: run a ninety‑day AI project.
premise: You lead a fictional airline's project to build an AI assistant that rebooks stranded passengers. The project has ninety days. You make thirteen decisions, and each one costs days.
pitch: A game takes ten to fifteen minutes. Every decision shows its price in days before you choose. Some decisions cost more days later.
short: SkyWays is a fictional airline building an assistant that rebooks stranded passengers.

line.caption: Start at Day 1, or press a day on the line to start there. The days before that day are played for you, the recommended way.
line.book: played for you the recommended way.
line.first: Or start at Day {day}, your first call

brief.calls: The calls, each with its price in days
brief.filed: On file, with the day each was filed
brief.spare: The project began with {n} spare days. The days before used {used}.
brief.owed: Nothing comes due from the days before.

building.caption: SkyWays head office. Each day happens in one room, lit. Day 1 is in the boardroom at the top. The days work down the floors to the passengers, and come back to the boardroom on Day 90.
building.key: Who works where, and their days

pressure.text: The booking-system vendor freezes changes for a week.

pm.name: Product manager
pm.line: You own what it is worth and what goes to the sponsor.

card.decide: You own what it is worth, and what the sponsor is told.
card.leave: a slide with the cost on it
card.pick: Pick this if you have to say what an AI project bought.

sa.name: Solution architect
sa.line: You own the requirements, the limits and the decisions that cut both ways.

card.decide: You own the requirements, the limits and the hard choices.
card.pick: Pick this if you turn what people ask for into a design.

eng.name: Engineering lead
eng.line: You own what ships, in what order, and who reads it first.

card.decide: You own what ships, in what order, and who reads it first.
card.pick: Pick this if your team ships code that an AI helped to write.

qa.name: QA lead
qa.line: You own the proof: what the number is, and what it is not.

card.decide: You own the proof: what the number is, and what it is not.
card.leave: a pass mark per kind of case
card.pick: Pick this if you are asked whether a number is good enough.

ops.name: Platform lead
ops.line: You own the gateway, the bill and the limits that live in code.

card.decide: You own the gateway, the bill and the limits in the code.
card.pick: Pick this if you run the platform the model calls go through.

card.decide: You set three rules, then watch the team work.
card.pick: Pick this if you fund AI projects, or decide what they must prove.

org.way: You are the sponsor. Pick three rules for the programme, then watch the ninety days run.
org.intro: You cannot enforce everything: a rule that stops the work costs days, and people route around the tenth one. Pick three. The team does the rest by habit.

register.name: Requirements register
register.plain: One list of what was asked for, each line with who asked and why.
register.on: The requirements list is on file.
register.off: No requirements list is on file.

credited.name: Credited list, confirmed
credited.plain: The list sent back with names on it, so merging duplicates costs nobody their credit.
credited.on: The confirmed list is on file.
credited.off: No confirmed list is on file.

constraints.name: Constraints, sorted by kind
constraints.plain: The limits you cannot negotiate: technical, legal and commercial.
constraints.on: The sorted limits are on file.
constraints.off: No sorted limits are on file.

targets.name: Signed quality targets
targets.plain: Non-functional requirements: how fast, how safe, how cheap. Signed by the people who own them.
targets.on: The signed quality targets are on file.
targets.off: No signed quality targets are on file.

records.name: Decision records
records.plain: One page per real trade-off: what was chosen and what was given up.
records.on: The decision records are on file.
records.off: No decision records are on file.

spec.name: Eight-field spec
spec.plain: What the assistant may do, how right it must be, and who signs, in a form a coding agent can read.
spec.on: The signed page is on file.
spec.off: No signed page is on file.

bar.name: Acceptance bar per kind of case
bar.plain: How often the assistant must be right, for each kind of case (a slice), worked out from what a mistake costs.
bar.on: A pass mark per kind of case is on file.
bar.off: No pass mark per kind of case is on file.

budget.name: Authority budget
budget.plain: What the assistant may do alone, and the limit on each action, signed.
budget.on: The limit on each action is on file.
budget.off: No limit on each action is on file.

matrix.name: Framework decision, with a way out
matrix.plain: Options scored on agreed criteria, with the three-year cost and what reversing it would take.
matrix.on: The framework decision is on file.
matrix.off: No framework decision is on file.

skeleton.name: Walking skeleton
skeleton.plain: The thinnest version that runs end to end, with no model in it, so the plumbing is proven first.
skeleton.on: The thin end-to-end version is on file.
skeleton.off: No thin end-to-end version is on file.

proof.name: Score with its margin, per kind of case
proof.plain: A score from a sample is a range. The low end of the range is what has been proven.
proof.on: The score with its margin is on file.
proof.off: No score with its margin is on file.

lanes.name: Review lanes by risk
lanes.plain: Two readers for changes that move money, one for behaviour, automatic checks alone for the rest.
lanes.on: The review lanes are on file.
lanes.off: No review lanes are on file.

rootcause.name: Root cause: four habits
rootcause.plain: One line per model call. It shows behaviour, where the invoice shows only the total.
rootcause.on: The cause of the bill is on file.
rootcause.off: No cause of the bill is on file.

control.name: Postmortem, and the control
control.plain: A limit the code enforces. A rule the model reads only lowers the odds.
control.on: The review of the refund is on file.
control.off: No review of the refund is on file.

report.name: Two-number report
report.plain: What was saved and what was spent, on one line, every cycle.
report.on: The two-number report is on file.
report.off: No two-number report is on file.

days.head: Six airline managers have given the project team 31 requirements for the AI assistant. Design starts this week.
days.context: It is the first week, and the project team has met the six managers twice.
scene: Six people gave us 31 requirements. Four of them are one requirement, said four ways.
days.ask: What should the team do with the 31 requirements?

options.label: Start the design from the 31 as written
options.recap: started the design from all 31 requests
options.now: Design starts this afternoon.

debt.text: The first design review became an argument about which line wins. The quiet stakeholder held the rule that mattered.

options.label: Merge them into one list that keeps who asked
options.recap: merged 31 requests into one list of 12
options.now: 31 lines become 12 requirements and 9 quality targets, with the limits still unsorted. Each keeps its source. Compliance has no line yet, and now the gap shows.

deeper: The two discovery meetings, in full

days.head: Six airline managers must approve one list of their 31 requirements. No manager has seen the list yet.
days.context: The project team wrote the list after two meetings with the six managers.
scene: I have the list. The six of them have not seen it.
Each of them will look for their own words first.
days.ask: What should the team send to the six managers?

options.label: The full minutes of both meetings
options.recap: sent out the full minutes of both meetings
options.now: Eleven pages go out. One of the six replies.

debt.text: Silence was taken as agreement. In week five it turned out that it was not.

options.label: The list, each line credited to who raised it
options.recap: sent six managers the requirements list, with their names
options.now: Four people see their words merged into one line, with their names beside it. All six confirm by Friday.

days.head: Three things set limits on the AI assistant: a refund law, a slow booking system and a partner airline contract.
days.context: The six managers have not yet agreed any target for speed, safety or cost.

leans.on: All six have confirmed the list.

scene: Every refund over $400 needs a named approver. That one is the law.
The booking system is old and slow. And our partners cap how often we can call them.
days.ask: When should the team set the three limits against the targets for speed, safety and cost?

options.label: After the targets are agreed, in one pass
options.recap: left the three limits on the assistant for later
options.now: The limits go in a folder for later.

debt.text: The room agreed a response time the old booking system cannot deliver. The workshop has to run again.

options.label: Now, sorted by kind, before anything is agreed
options.recap: sorted the limits on the assistant before agreeing any target
options.now: The limits come out of the folder before the workshop. Six lines were called a must in the meetings, and some of them are only wishes.

deeper: Constraints, and the targets they reshape

days.head: The AI assistant has nine quality targets, such as speed and cost. The nine targets cannot all come first.
days.context: Six airline managers have one afternoon to put the nine targets in order.
scene: Nine quality targets, six people, one afternoon.
days.ask: How should the six managers decide which target comes first?

options.label: Dots on a wall: everyone votes, and the count decides
options.recap: let a dot vote rank the nine quality targets
options.now: The room is done by three o'clock. Cost per case gets two dots.

debt.text: Nobody set an alert on cost, because the vote put it last. The bill grew for weeks before anyone looked.

options.label: Each person ranks what matters and what is hard; merge the six
options.recap: had six managers rank the nine quality targets
options.now: Nine targets, signed. Three score high on both importance and difficulty. Those three are where a design decision is owed.

days.head: The AI assistant's design has three hard decisions. Each decision gains one thing and gives up another, and no decision is written down.
days.context: Design has started, and the team has never recorded a design decision in writing.

leans.on: Three of them need a design decision.

scene: Three of our decisions cut both ways. The team has never written one down.
So how many do we write?
days.ask: How many of its design decisions should the team record in writing?

options.label: One for every design choice the team has made
options.recap: wrote forty decision records, one per design choice
options.now: Forty records by Friday.

debt.text: Nobody read the forty-first record. The three that mattered are buried, so the framework choice starts from nothing.

options.label: One for each real trade-off; the rest go in a design note
options.recap: wrote a decision record for each real trade-off
options.now: Two are written today and the third is dated for week three. Each names what was given up.

days.signoff: This is the one hand-off that stops the work. Nothing is built until three documents are signed. After today, changing your mind costs a rewrite.
days.head: Today the product manager signs off what the AI assistant must do. The engineers will build exactly what is signed.
days.context: The requirements run to thirty pages, and the engineers' coding agent builds whatever it is given.
scene: The requirements document is thirty pages.
My coding agent will read none of it. It builds what it is given, to the letter.
days.ask: Which document should the engineers build the AI assistant from?

options.label: The thirty pages, with a summary on top
options.recap: started the build from thirty pages and a summary
options.now: The build can start on Monday. How much the assistant may do alone is left to whoever writes the code.
options.after: Nobody decided what the assistant may pay out alone. It came back on Day 82.

options.label: One page: what it may do, how right it must be, who signs
options.recap: cut the thirty-page requirements to one signed page
options.now: Five things turned out to be undecided: the model's role, what it may do alone, how right it must be, the fallback, the records. Each is settled with its owner.

options.label: Stop everything until every open question is closed
options.recap: stopped all work until every open question was closed
options.now: Eleven meetings. Eight of those questions could have run beside the build, each with an owner and a date.
options.after: Five days, where two would have done.

deeper: Does this decision stop the work?

days.head: The AI assistant needs a software framework to run on. The team can build a framework, buy one or borrow a free one.
days.context: The engineering lead already favours one framework, and the choice will last for years.

leans.on: The third one, the framework, is due today.

scene: We can build the agent framework, buy one, or borrow an open one. I know which I like.
Liking it is not a reason we can defend in a year.
days.ask: How should the team choose the framework?

options.label: Go with the most senior engineer's choice
options.recap: took the senior engineer's favourite framework
options.now: Chosen in ten minutes.

debt.text: Nobody can say why this framework was chosen, so the incident reopens the choice.

options.label: Score the three on the signed targets and the cost over three years
options.recap: scored three frameworks on the signed targets
options.now: The criteria come from the signed targets, so the weights are already agreed. The record names what reversing the choice would take.

options.label: Pause the build until all three are trialled
options.recap: paused the build to trial all three frameworks
options.now: Three trials, six working days. The answer matches the scoring.
options.after: Six days, for the answer the scoring gave.

days.head: The engineers start building the AI assistant today. Seven things about the build are still unknown.
days.context: Design is finished, and the first two weeks of building are already booked.
scene: Seven things we do not know yet, and a two-week sprint already on the calendar.
days.ask: What should the engineers build first?

options.label: The model call, drafting a reply to one real case
options.recap: built the model call first, on one real case
options.now: A draft reply appears on day two. It is wrong, and it is not clear why.

debt.text: When the draft was wrong it could have been the prompt, the booking adapter or the search tool. Three days went on telling them apart.

options.label: The thinnest version that runs end to end, with no model in it
options.recap: built the thinnest end-to-end version first
options.now: A booking shows on a screen by four in the afternoon. The plumbing is proven, and each day after retires one unknown.

deeper: Plan the build one proven piece at a time

days.head: On its first test the AI assistant got 82.4 percent of 500 real cases right. The team promised 80 percent.
days.context: The assistant is due to start answering real passengers on Monday.
scene: 500 real cases. 412 right. That is 82.4 percent.
And we promised 80. So we pass?
days.ask: What should the QA lead report about the score?

options.label: A pass: 82.4 beats the 80 we promised
options.recap: reported 82.4 as a pass, with no margin
options.now: Everything goes to 5 percent of passengers on Monday.

debt.tag: a pass, with no margin stated
debt.text: The live rate read 80. It was always inside the margin. The team spent a fortnight hunting a fault that was not there.

options.label: 82.4, at least 79.1, then each kind of case on its own
options.recap: reported 82.4 with its margin, one kind at a time
options.now: Probably above the bar, and not yet proven. Saying so is what makes the next number believable.

options.label: Hold every kind of case until it clears one bar of 98
options.recap: held every kind of case to one bar of 98
options.now: Nothing ships. Same-day changes were ready weeks ago and wait with the rest.
options.after: The work that was ready waited. It shows in what was saved.

deeper: Has a score proven the bar?

days.head: Nine changes to the AI assistant's code are waiting to be reviewed. Two of the nine changes alter how refunds are paid.
days.context: Two senior engineers read every change, and the queue is four days long.

leans.on: The build has added a piece a day since.

scene: Nine changes are waiting for review. The queue is four days long.
Two of the nine touch money.
days.ask: How should the team review the nine changes?

options.label: Ask the reviewers to go faster until the queue clears
options.recap: asked the reviewers to read faster
options.now: They do, for a week.

debt.text: The change that touched the refund limit got a ninety-second reading on a Friday. It has to be pulled back and read again.

options.label: Route by risk: two readers, one, or the automatic checks alone
options.recap: sent the nine changes to review by risk
options.now: The two money changes are read first, by people who are no longer tired.

options.label: Keep two senior readers on every change
options.recap: kept two senior readers on every change
options.now: Nothing changes. Every change still waits for the same two people.

debt.text: The queue kept growing. Three fixes sat behind a typo correction.

deeper: How long does a change wait?

days.head: The bill for the assistant's AI model is 4.4 times the estimate. Passenger numbers are flat.
days.context: The assistant now answers real passengers, and the funding decision is fifteen days away.

leans.on: One is a limit on cost per case.

scene: The model bill is 4.4 times the estimate. Traffic is flat.
days.ask: What should the team look at first to explain the bill?

options.label: A comparison of cheaper models
options.recap: opened a comparison of cheaper models
options.now: Three weeks of trials. The habits behind the bill carry on at a lower unit price.

debt.text: Finance asks why the bill is still more than twice the estimate. Nobody can say which habit is behind it.

options.label: The log of every model call
options.recap: opened the log of every model call
options.now: Four things moved, and they multiply: 1.6 × 1.5 × 1.3 × 1.41 is 4.4. That is the whole bill.

options.label: Switch the assistant off until it is understood
options.recap: switched the assistant off for a week
options.now: The assistant is off for a week. The contact centre goes back to the phones.

debt.text: A week back on the phones. The contact-centre head brings it up in the room, and the bill was never explained.

days.context: By law, a refund over $400 needs a named person to approve it.

leans.on: A $400 limit on refunds was signed then.
leans.off: No limit on refunds was signed then.

blocked.fig: The $400 limit is in the refund tool itself. That is a wall, and the refund stopped at it.
blocked.head: The AI assistant tried to refund $2,000 to a passenger who was owed $180. The refund tool refused the payment.
scene: A passenger was owed $180. The assistant tried to refund $2,000.
The tool refused it at $400. The limit is in the code.
blocked.ask: What should the team do about the refund that was refused?

options.label: Close the case as blocked
options.recap: closed the refused refund unread
options.now: The case is closed. Nobody asks why the assistant wanted $2,000.

debt.text: Ines asks what was learned from the refund that was refused. Nothing was written down.

options.label: Add the case to the test set, and review what it may do alone
options.recap: added the refused refund to the test set
options.now: Six cases like it join the test set. The limit held, and now there is a test that says so every week.

paid.fig: The $400 limit was a sentence in the prompt. That is paper, and the refund went through it.
paid.head: The AI assistant paid $2,000 to a passenger who was owed $180. Nothing stopped the payment.
scene: A passenger was sent a $2,000 refund that was not owed.
The $400 limit was written in the prompt. The refund tool accepts any amount.
paid.ask: What should the review of the wrong payment ask first?

options.label: Who wrote that prompt, and who approved it?
options.recap: asked who wrote and approved the prompt
options.now: A name is found and a training session is booked.

debt.text: The refund tool still accepted any amount. It happened again in week thirteen.

options.label: What limit in the code would have made this impossible?
options.recap: put the refund limit into the tool itself
options.now: A limit and a confirmation step go into the tool itself. The assistant may do one level less alone. Six cases like it join the test set.

deeper: Which control does each tool carry?

days.head: The executive who sponsors the project asks what ninety days achieved and what the work cost.
days.context: A committee of airline executives decides today whether to keep funding the assistant.
scene: Ninety days. What did we get, and what did it cost?
days.ask: The slide for the committee has room for three lines. Which three should go on the slide?

limits.title: Which of these can move?
limits.intro: All six were called a must in the meetings. Tick what nobody in this building can change inside ninety days. Everything left unticked goes to the Day 9 workshop to be ranked.

lines.text: Refunds over $400 need a named approver.
lines.bends: Refunds: a named approver signs anything over $400.

miss.tag: a law, sent to the workshop as a wish
miss.text: Compliance stopped the sign-off. The rule on refunds over $400 is the law, and the workshop had ranked it like a wish.

lines.text: It must answer in five seconds.
The booking system is slow and is not being replaced.
lines.bends: Speed: 30 seconds for 95 in 100 requests, which the old system can meet.

lines.text: It must never hand a passenger to a person.
Partner airlines cap how often we may call them.
lines.bends: Partner flights: partner seats cached inside the cap.

miss.tag: the partners' cap, sent to the workshop as a wish
miss.text: A partner airline cut off the first build. It had called their system more often than the contract allows.

lines.text: It must cost less per case than a phone call.

wish.tag: a wish, filed as a fixed limit
wish.text: A wish had been filed as a limit nobody could move. The workshop spent a day finding out that it could.

bar.title: Set the bar
bar.intro: How often must it be right? Divide what a wrong answer costs by what a right one saves. If a wrong one costs four times as much, it has to be right four times in five.
bar.hold: A person approves each refund before it goes out

after.held: With a person on refunds, a wrong one costs $30, not $600. The bar for refunds falls from 98 to 71.
after.unheld: With nobody checking refunds, a wrong one costs $600. The bar for refunds is 98, which no model on this floor will reach.

score.title: Read the score, one kind of case at a time
score.intro: The 500 cases are three kinds of work. For each: ship it to 5 percent of passengers, run it beside the desk with no effect, or keep it with people.

route.title: Route the nine changes
route.intro: Each change gets two readers, one reader, or the automatic checks alone.

items.name: Raise the refund limit for delays over six hours
Fix a typo in a log message
Change who may approve a refund
Reword the apology in the delay reply
Add a tool that reads the seat map
Add six cases to the test set
Retry the booking system once on a timeout
Rename a variable in the search tool

leak.title: Find the leak
leak.intro: The log, against the numbers from the trial run. You have one day. Which fixes go first?

rows.name: Tokens sent per call
rows.why: the whole booking history is pasted in

rows.name: Calls sent to the dearest model
rows.why: set "to be safe" after one complaint
rows.fix: Restore routing by kind of case

rows.name: Calls that reuse the stored start of the prompt
rows.why: the model is switched inside a session

rows.name: Retries per conversation
rows.why: a retry loop with no limit
rows.fix: Add a limit of five tries

slide.title: Build the slide
slide.intro: Three lines fit. Finance has the invoice.

policies.name: Nothing is built until what it may do, how right, and its limits are signed
Requirements and targets are confirmed by the people who own them
Nothing ships on a score alone: its margin is stated too
Every limit lives in the tool that enforces it
How much process a change gets follows its risk
Every report carries what was saved and what was spent

monday: Is the limit in the tool, or only in the prompt?
What is the least that score could be, and on how many cases?
Which of our open decisions really stops the work?

funded.name: Funded for a second cycle
funded.line: The room stopped asking whether this is real and started asking what you need next.

conditional.name: Funded, with conditions
conditional.line: The programme continues. The sponsor wants the open items closed before any more passengers are added.

paused.name: Paused for review
paused.line: Nobody doubts the effort. The committee cannot tell what it bought.

stopped.name: Stopped
stopped.line: The assistant is switched off. The next proposal will have to answer for this one.
